solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which x > 0.
steps: The condition x > 0 places P to the right of the y-axis.
Since x is strictly positive, P cannot lie on the y-axis.
There is no restriction on y, so P may be above, below, or on the x-axis.
solutions.answer: P lies in the open right half-plane, excluding the y-axis.
solutions.note: Your textbook's answer key shows "Right half plane and negative y-axis"; the checked working above gives this answer.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which x > 0 and y > 0.
steps: Since x > 0, P lies to the right of the y-axis.
Since y > 0, P lies above the x-axis.
Therefore, P lies in the 1st quadrant.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which y = 0.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which x > 0 and y ≤ 0.
steps: The condition x > 0 places P to the right of the y-axis.
The condition y < 0 places P in the fourth quadrant.
The condition y = 0 places P on the positive x-axis; since x > 0, the origin is excluded.
solutions.answer: P lies in the fourth quadrant or on the positive x-axis, excluding the origin.
solutions.note: Your textbook's answer key shows "4th quadrant"; the checked working above gives this answer.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which y = 0, x = 0.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which x = y.
steps: Since x = y, the points have equal x- and y-coordinates.
The set of such points lies on a straight line through the origin.
This line bisects the 1st and 3rd quadrants.
solutions.answer: It is a line bisecting 1st and 3rd quadrant.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which x ≥ 3.
steps: Since x ≥ 3, the x-coordinate of P is 3 or greater.
When x = 3, P lies on the line x = 3.
When x > 3, P lies to the right of the line x = 3.
Therefore, the set consists of the points on and to the right of the line x = 3.
solutions.answer: The set of points lying on and right side of the line x = 3.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which y > 0.
steps: Since y > 0, the ordinate of P is positive.
Therefore, P lies above the x-axis.
solutions.answer: The set of points lying above the x-axis.

solutions.question: Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y), for which x and y have opposite signs.
steps: When x and y have opposite signs, either x < 0 and y > 0, or x > 0 and y < 0.
If x < 0 and y > 0, P lies in the second quadrant.
If x > 0 and y < 0, P lies in the fourth quadrant.
Therefore, the points lie in the second and fourth quadrants.
solutions.answer: The set of points in the second and fourth quadrants.

solutions.question: By means of slopes, show that the following points lie on the same line: X(a, 2b); Y(c, a + b); Z(2c − a, 2a).

If c ≠ a, slope of XY = ((a + b) − 2b)/(c − a) = (a − b)/(c − a).
If c ≠ a, slope of XZ = (2a − 2b)/((2c − a) − a) = 2(a − b)/(2(c − a)) = (a − b)/(c − a).
Thus, when c ≠ a, slope of XY = slope of XZ, so X, Y, and Z lie on the same line.
If c = a, the x-coordinates of X, Y, and Z are a, a, and 2a − a = a, respectively.
Thus, when c = a, all three points lie on the vertical line x = a.
Therefore, for all values of a, b, and c, X, Y, and Z lie on the same line.
solutions.answer: X, Y, and Z lie on the same line.

solutions.question: Two pairs of points are given. Find whether the two lines determined by these points are (i) parallel (ii) perpendicular (iii) none: (1, −2), (2, 4) and (4, 1), (−8, 2).
steps: Slope of the line through (1, −2) and (2, 4), m₁ = (4 − (−2))/(2 − 1) = 6.
Slope of the line through (4, 1) and (−8, 2), m₂ = (2 − 1)/(−8 − 4) = −1/12.
Since m₁ ≠ m₂, the lines are not parallel.
Also, m₁m₂ = 6(−1/12) = −1/2 ≠ −1, so the lines are not perpendicular.
solutions.answer: The lines are neither parallel nor perpendicular.
